pages.title: EU data policy
pages.blurb: How Festival Planner handles personal data under the GDPR: it does not collect any.

body.v: Festival Planner has no accounts, no analytics, no advertising and no tracking. It collects no personal data about you at all. This page explains what that means in practice and what little data still moves when you load a page.
Who is responsible
Festival Planner is a personal, non-commercial project run from Helsinki. For anything on this page, write to __CONTACT__.
What is stored on your device

When you add a set to your plan on a planner page, that choice is written to your own browser — as a cookie where the site is hosted, or as a localStorage entry when the page is opened from a file. It holds nothing but the identifiers of the sets you picked.

v: It is never transmitted anywhere. There is no server to send it to.
It is not readable by any other site.
It carries no identifier for you, your device or your browser.
Clearing your browser's site data for this domain removes it completely.

body.v: Under the ePrivacy rules this is storage strictly necessary for a feature you asked for. It is not used for analytics or advertising, which is why the notice on the planner pages explains what it does rather than asking you to consent to tracking.
What leaves your browser

Every page on this site is a single self-contained file. Fonts, maps, artwork and code are embedded in it, so once a page has loaded it makes no further network requests — no font CDN, no image host, no analytics endpoint. You can disconnect and it keeps working.
Two things are unavoidable:

v: Hosting. The site is served by GitHub Pages. To deliver a page, GitHub necessarily processes your IP address and request metadata, and may retain it briefly for security and abuse prevention. This is GitHub's processing, not ours, and is covered by the GitHub Privacy Statement. We receive none of it and have no access to any log.

Links you choose to follow. Ticket sellers, festival sites, streaming services and map data sources are separate companies with their own policies. Following a link there is a visit to them, and nothing about your plan travels with you.

body.v: Location

The place selector in the header reads Finland by default and does nothing on its own. If you press Use my location, your browser asks your permission and, if you grant it, hands the page a coordinate.

v: The coordinate is used once, immediately, to work out which of the places on that short list is nearest.
It is not stored. Only the name of the place you ended up on is kept, in your own browser.
It is not transmitted. There is no server to send it to, and the page makes no network requests.
Declining the permission prompt costs you nothing — pick a place from the list instead.

body.v: Information about performing artists

The planner pages name the artists who are booked to play, and for some of them show a portrait, a short description and links to their own streaming or social pages. Where an artist is an individual rather than a band or a company, that counts as personal data under the GDPR, so it is worth being explicit about how it is handled.

v: What is shown. Stage name, set time and stage, a genre tag, a publicity photograph, a short professional blurb and links the artist already publishes. Nothing else — no contact details, no private-life information, and no special category data.

Where it comes from. Each festival's own public programme page for that act, plus the public MusicBrainz and Deezer catalogues. All of it is material published deliberately, by the artist or their organiser, to promote a publicly advertised performance.

Legal basis. Legitimate interests, Article 6(1)(f) — describing a public event accurately to people deciding whether to attend. The processing is limited to professional information the artist has already made public in that professional capacity, which is why it does not override their interests or rights.
What is not done. No profiles are built, nothing is combined with data about you, nothing is used for advertising or sold, and none of it is transferred outside the page you are reading.

body.v: If you are a performing artist and you would like your photograph, description or listing removed or changed, write to __CONTACT__. This is your Article 21 right to object, and it is honoured on request without you having to give reasons — acknowledged within 3 days and actioned within 7. Your set time may stay listed as a plain fact about the event, unless you tell us you would rather it did not appear at all.
Your rights

The GDPR gives you the right to access, rectify, erase, restrict and port your personal data, to object to processing, and to complain to a supervisory authority — in Finland, the Office of the Data Protection Ombudsman.

As a visitor, there is nothing here to exercise those rights against. We hold no personal data about you, so there is no record to hand over, correct or delete. The only data connected to you sits in your own browser, under your own control, and you can erase it yourself at any time. Performing artists named on the planner pages are the one exception, and the section above sets out how to exercise these rights over that material.
Children
The site is open to anyone and collects nothing from anyone, so it needs no age gate and holds no children's data.
Changes
If this ever stops being accurate — if anything is added that does collect data — this page will be updated before that change ships, and the date at the top will say so.

pages.title: Terms and Conditions
pages.blurb: The terms covering use of the Festival Planner site, including its unofficial status and the limits of its accuracy.

body.v: Festival Planner is a free, unofficial tool. These terms describe what it is, what it is not, and what you can rely on it for.
1. Unofficial and unaffiliated

This site is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to any of the festivals it covers, their organisers, promoters, venues or ticket sellers. It is an independent project that reads publicly published schedules and lays them out so they can be planned against.
2. Accuracy

Timetables are transcribed by hand from each organiser's own published schedule and checked against secondary sources where they exist. Care is taken, but errors are possible, and lineups change: sets get moved, stages get renamed, artists cancel.
Always check the organiser's official schedule before you travel. This site is a planning aid, not a source of truth. Where it disagrees with the organiser, the organiser is right.
The site is provided as is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied, including any warranty of accuracy, completeness or fitness for a particular purpose.
3. Liability

To the fullest extent permitted by law, no liability is accepted for any loss arising from use of this site — including a set you missed, a ticket you bought, or a journey you made on the strength of something shown here. Nothing in these terms limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or for fraud, where such limits cannot lawfully be excluded.
4. Trade marks and artwork

Festival names, logos, posters and artist images belong to their respective owners. They appear here solely to identify the festival or artist a listing refers to, which is a descriptive use, and no claim of ownership or endorsement is made or implied.
If you hold rights in material shown here and would like it removed or credited differently, write to __CONTACT__ and it will be dealt with promptly.
5. Links to other sites

Links to official festival sites, ticket sellers and streaming services are provided for convenience. Those sites are outside our control, and we are not responsible for their content, their availability, or anything you buy through them.
6. Acceptable use
You are welcome to use the site for personal planning, to share links to it, and to open it offline. Please do not present it as an official schedule, or republish it in a way that implies it is.
7. Changes
These terms may be updated as the site changes. The date at the top of this page reflects the current version. Continued use after a change means you accept the revised terms.
8. Governing law
These terms are governed by Finnish law. If any provision is found unenforceable, the rest continues to apply.

pages.title: About us
pages.blurb: Why Festival Planner exists, how it is built, and who is behind it.

body.v: Festival Planner turns Helsinki festival schedules into something you can actually plan against.
The problem

Most festivals publish their timetable as a poster — a single image, or a PDF laid out for print. It looks good and it is nearly useless on the day. You cannot search it, you cannot tell which of two sets you would have to give up, and you certainly cannot work out whether you can get from one stage to another in the eight minutes between them.
What this is
One page per festival, built around a real timetable grid: stages down the side, hours across the top, every set in its true position. From there you can:

v: Filter by genre, or search for an artist by name.
Open any act to see who they are and hear them before you commit an hour to them.
Build a personal route, and see immediately where two picks collide.
Find the stage on an interactive map with pins placed against real streets.

body.v: How it is built

Each planner is a single self-contained HTML file. Fonts, maps, artwork and code are all embedded in it. That has one consequence that matters at a festival: once the page has loaded, it keeps working with no signal at all — in a basement, in a field, or on a phone with a dead data plan.

It also means nothing is watching you use it. There is no server, no account and no analytics. Your plan is saved on your own device and goes nowhere. The EU data policy sets out exactly what that means.
Sources and rights

Everything here is compiled from material each organiser has already published openly on their own website. Nothing is taken from behind a login or a paywall, and no schedule is republished wholesale: set times are re-laid-out as a grid you can plan against, and every listing points back to the organiser's own page. Where a source and the organiser disagree, the organiser wins.
Per festival, in detail:

v: Flow Festival 2026 — timetable, stage names and set times from the published schedule at flowfestival.com/en/schedule. Artist descriptions, streaming links and portraits come from each act's own page on the same site. Ticket links go to the official shop; we sell nothing and take no commission.
Kallio Block Party 2026 — timetable, stage list and lineup from the published programme at kallioblockparty.org. The festival is free and volunteer-run, and there is no ticketing to link to.

body.v: Shared sources, used across every planner:

v: Artist links and genre tags — the public MusicBrainz database and Deezer's public API, with cover art from the iTunes Search API. A match is only accepted when the returned artist name is an exact match for the booked name, so an unmatched act gets a generated cover rather than a stranger's face.
Maps — map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, tiles by CARTO, both used under their own licences. Stage pins are placed by hand against the streets the stages actually sit on.
Fonts and code — open-licensed typefaces, embedded in the page. No third-party scripts, no ad network, no analytics.

body.v: Festival names, logos, posters and artist photographs remain the property of their owners. They appear here only to identify the festival or artist a listing refers to — a descriptive use — and no ownership, endorsement or affiliation is claimed or implied. See the Terms and Conditions for the full position.
Corrections and takedown requests

If you are an organiser, an artist, a photographer or any other rights holder and you want something changed, credited differently or taken down, you do not need a lawyer and you do not need to explain yourself at length. One email is enough.

Write to __CONTACT__ with the subject line Takedown request. It helps if you can include the page and the exact item (an image, a listing, a stage name, or the whole festival), and one line on what you would like done — removed, replaced, or credited a particular way.

Every request is actioned in good faith: an acknowledgement within 3 days and the change published within 7 days, normally the same day. Removal is not conditional on you proving ownership — if you ask, it comes down, and any disagreement can be sorted out afterwards.
The same address takes ordinary corrections. A wrong set time, a misspelled artist, a stage pin in the wrong place — all worth reporting, and all get fixed.
Get in touch
Corrections are genuinely welcome — a wrong set time is worth reporting, and it will be fixed. Requests for a festival that is not covered yet are welcome too.
Write to __CONTACT__.
